documentation.text:
@title  ProductRegistry
 @notice Layer-1 of the anti-counterfeiting system.
 Design decisions (see docs/DECISIONS.md for rationale):
  - No strings stored on-chain. Everything is a bytes32 hash.
  - Product details, images, and QR/NFC payloads live off-chain (backend DB).
  - Owner manages a manufacturer whitelist.
  - A separate "operator" account (the backend) is the only caller allowed
    to record scan verdicts via logScan().
  - No unbounded loops. All mappings are keyed by productId.
  - Verdict codes: 0 = Verified, 1 = ManualReview, 2 = Suspicious, 3 = Unregistered.

@param _operator  Address of the backend account that will call logScan().
                   Can be the same as owner during development.
@notice Add an address to the manufacturer whitelist.
@notice Remove an address from the manufacturer whitelist.

params.scanHash: Hash of (productId + channel + deviceHash + lat + lon + timestamp)                   computed by the backend so raw PII never touches the chain.

params._operator: Address of the backend account that will call logScan().                   Can be the same as owner during development.

returns.exists: False if the productId was never registered.

params.productId: The scanned product (may not exist – verdict 3 in that case).

markSold(bytes32).details: The modifier here is onlyOperator; manufacturers call /sell via the API         which uses the operator key. Change to onlyManufacturer if needed.

params.recordHash: SHA-256 hash of the off-chain JSON record (product details + image hash).

addManufacturer(address).notice: Add an address to the manufacturer whitelist.

markSold(bytes32).notice: Mark a product as sold. Can only move from not-sold → sold.         Called by the backend operator (or a whitelisted manufacturer).         We allow both so the frontend can call it without routing through backend.

removeManufacturer(address).notice: Remove an address from the manufacturer whitelist.

userdoc.notice: Layer-1 of the anti-counterfeiting system. Design decisions (see docs/DECISIONS.md for rationale):  - No strings stored on-chain. Everything is a bytes32 hash.  - Product details, images, and QR/NFC payloads live off-chain (backend DB).  - Owner manages a manufacturer whitelist.  - A separate "operator" account (the backend) is the only caller allowed    to record scan verdicts via logScan().  - No unbounded loops. All mappings are keyed by productId.  - Verdict codes: 0 = Verified, 1 = ManualReview, 2 = Suspicious, 3 = Unregistered.
